newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to set new Thomson sale terms this week.
newsitem.headline: France to set new Thomson sale terms this week.

text.p: The French government will unveil this week new terms for the privatisation of electronics group Thomson SA, one week after its shock decision to suspend the politically sensitive sale, sources said Tuesday

Government sources said that the new terms would be announced by the end of the week. Industrial sources said a statement could be made as soon as Wednesday or Thursday -- ahead of a televised interview with President Jacques Chirac that evening.
"The aim of the government is to announce new terms between now and the end of the week," an official source said.
Budget Minister Alain Lamassoure told parliament that the new terms would be announced soon but he did not give a specific time.

"We have decided to go quickly because a company as important as (Thomson) can not stay too long in uncertainty," Lamassoure told parliament. "That is why we have decided that the government will set out very soon the new terms and timetable for the privatisation of Thomson."

Prime Minister Alain Juppe said Monday that the group's 58 percent stake in defence electronics group Thomson-CSF might be sold separately from the fully-owned consumer electronics unit Thomson Multimedia.
In February, announcing the original sale plans, Chirac said the Thomson group needed to be sold as one entity.
The government announced Oct. 16 it had preferred an offer by defence group Lagardere over one by electrical engineering group Alcatel-Alsthom.

France was to have sold indebted Thomson SA for one franc to Lagardere after an 10.8 billion franc ($2.06 billion) capital increase. Lagardere would have sold Thomson Multimedia, also for one symbolic franc, to Daewoo Electronics, which promised investments and the creation of thousands of new jobs in France.

However, the independent Privatisation Commission said it objected to the terms of the sale to Daewoo, effectively blocking the privatisation plans and forcing the government into a politically embarassing U-turn.
